1.speaker: job
1.quote: “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.”

1.speaker: satan
1.quote: “From roaming throughout the earth, going back and forth on it.”

1.speaker: the-lord
1.quote: “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil.”

1.speaker: satan
1.quote: “Have you not put a hedge around him and his household and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, so that his flocks and herds are spread throughout the land.

1.speaker: satan
1.quote: But now stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face.”

1.speaker: the-lord
1.quote: “Very well, then, everything he has is in your power, but on the man himself do not lay a finger.”

1.speaker: messenger
1.quote: “The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,

1.speaker: messenger
1.quote: and the Sabeans attacked and made off with them. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

1.speaker: messenger
1.quote: “The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep and the servants, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

1.speaker: messenger
1.quote: “The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties and swept down on your camels and made off with them. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

1.speaker: messenger
1.quote: “Your sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother`s house,

1.speaker: messenger
1.quote: when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on them and they are dead, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”

1.speaker: job
1.quote: “Naked I came from my mother`s womb, and naked I will depart. The Lord gave and the Lord has taken away; may the name of the Lord be praised.”

2.speaker: satan
2.quote: “From roaming throughout the earth, going back and forth on it.”

2.speaker: the-lord
2.quote: “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil. And he still maintains his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without any reason.”

2.speaker: satan
2.quote: “A man will give all he has for his own life.

2.speaker: satan
2.quote: But now stretch out your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse you to your face.”

2.speaker: the-lord
2.quote: “Very well, then, he is in your hands; but you must spare his life.”

2.speaker: jobs-wife
2.quote: “Are you still maintaining your integrity? Curse God and die!”

2.speaker: job
2.quote: “You are talking like a foolish woman. Shall we accept good from God, and not trouble?”

3.speaker: job
3.quote: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night that said, ‘A boy is conceived!`

3.speaker: job
3.quote: That day—may it turn to darkness; may God above not care about it; may no light shine on it.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: May gloom and utter darkness claim it once more; may a cloud settle over it; may blackness overwhelm it.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: That night—may thick darkness seize it; may it not be included among the days of the year nor be entered in any of the months.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: May that night be barren; may no shout of joy be heard in it.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: May those who curse days curse that day, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: May its morning stars become dark; may it wait for daylight in vain and not see the first rays of dawn,

3.speaker: job
3.quote: for it did not shut the doors of the womb on me to hide trouble from my eyes.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: “Why did I not perish at birth, and die as I came from the womb?

3.speaker: job
3.quote: Why were there knees to receive me and breasts that I might be nursed?

3.speaker: job
3.quote: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest

3.speaker: job
3.quote: with kings and rulers of the earth, who built for themselves places now lying in ruins,

3.speaker: job
3.quote: with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: Or why was I not hidden away in the ground like a stillborn child, like an infant who never saw the light of day?

3.speaker: job
3.quote: There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary are at rest.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: Captives also enjoy their ease; they no longer hear the slave driver`s shout.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: The small and the great are there, and the slaves are freed from their owners.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: “Why is light given to those in misery, and life to the bitter of soul,

3.speaker: job
3.quote: to those who long for death that does not come, who search for it more than for hidden treasure,

3.speaker: job
3.quote: who are filled with gladness and rejoice when they reach the grave?

3.speaker: job
3.quote: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

3.speaker: job
3.quote: For sighing has become my daily food; my groans pour out like water.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: What I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has happened to me.

3.speaker: job
3.quote: I have no peace, no quietness; I have no rest, but only turmoil.”

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: “If someone ventures a word with you, will you be impatient? But who can keep from speaking?

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: Think how you have instructed many, how you have strengthened feeble hands.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: Your words have supported those who stumbled; you have strengthened faltering knees.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: But now trouble comes to you, and you are discouraged; it strikes you, and you are dismayed.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: Should not your piety be your confidence and your blameless ways your hope?

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: “Consider now: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Where were the upright ever destroyed?

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: As I have observed, those who plow evil and those who sow trouble reap it.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: At the breath of God they perish; at the blast of his anger they are no more.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: The lions may roar and growl, yet the teeth of the great lions are broken.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: The lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: “A word was secretly brought to me, my ears caught a whisper of it.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: Amid disquieting dreams in the night, when deep sleep falls on people,

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: fear and trembling seized me and made all my bones shake.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood on end.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: It stopped, but I could not tell what it was. A form stood before my eyes, and I heard a hushed voice:

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can even a strong man be more pure than his Maker?

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: If God places no trust in his servants, if he charges his angels with error,

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: how much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who are crushed more readily than a moth!

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: Between dawn and dusk they are broken to pieces; unnoticed, they perish forever.

4.speaker: eliphaz
4.quote: Are not the cords of their tent pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?`

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: “Call if you will, but who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: Resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: His children are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from among thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: For hardship does not spring from the soil, nor does trouble sprout from the ground.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: “But if I were you, I would appeal to God; I would lay my cause before him.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: He provides rain for the earth; he sends water on the countryside.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: The lowly he sets on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: He thwarts the plans of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and the schemes of the wily are swept away.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: Darkness comes upon them in the daytime; at noon they grope as in the night.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth; he saves them from the clutches of the powerful.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: “Blessed is the one whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: For he wounds, but he also binds up; he injures, but his hands also heal.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: From six calamities he will rescue you; in seven no harm will touch you.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: In famine he will deliver you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: You will be protected from the lash of the tongue, and need not fear when destruction comes.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the wild animals.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: You will know that your tent is secure; you will take stock of your property and find nothing missing.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: You will know that your children will be many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like sheaves gathered in season.

5.speaker: eliphaz
5.quote: “We have examined this, and it is true. So hear it and apply it to yourself.”

6.speaker: job
6.quote: “If only my anguish could be weighed and all my misery be placed on the scales!

6.speaker: job
6.quote: It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas— no wonder my words have been impetuous.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: The arrows of the Almighty are in me, my spirit drinks in their poison; God`s terrors are marshaled against me.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass, or an ox bellow when it has fodder?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the sap of the mallow?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: I refuse to touch it; such food makes me ill.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: “Oh, that I might have my request, that God would grant what I hope for,

6.speaker: job
6.quote: that God would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut off my life!

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Then I would still have this consolation— my joy in unrelenting pain— that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: “What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What prospects, that I should be patient?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Do I have the strength of stone? Is my flesh bronze?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Do I have any power to help myself, now that success has been driven from me?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: “Anyone who withholds kindness from a friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: But my brothers are as undependable as intermittent streams, as the streams that overflow

6.speaker: job
6.quote: when darkened by thawing ice and swollen with melting snow,

6.speaker: job
6.quote: but that stop flowing in the dry season, and in the heat vanish from their channels.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go off into the wasteland and perish.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: The caravans of Tema look for water, the traveling merchants of Sheba look in hope.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: They are distressed, because they had been confident; they arrive there, only to be disappointed.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Now you too have proved to be of no help; you see something dreadful and are afraid.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Have I ever said, ‘Give something on my behalf, pay a ransom for me from your wealth,

6.speaker: job
6.quote: deliver me from the hand of the enemy, rescue me from the clutches of the ruthless`?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: “Teach me, and I will be quiet; show me where I have been wrong.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: How painful are honest words! But what do your arguments prove?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Do you mean to correct what I say, and treat my desperate words as wind?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: You would even cast lots for the fatherless and barter away your friend.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: “But now be so kind as to look at me. Would I lie to your face?

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Relent, do not be unjust; reconsider, for my integrity is at stake.

6.speaker: job
6.quote: Is there any wickedness on my lips? Can my mouth not discern malice?

7.speaker: job
7.quote: “Do not mortals have hard service on earth? Are not their days like those of hired laborers?

7.speaker: job
7.quote: Like a slave longing for the evening shadows, or a hired laborer waiting to be paid,

7.speaker: job
7.quote: so I have been allotted months of futility, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: When I lie down I think, ‘How long before I get up?` The night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: My body is clothed with worms and scabs, my skin is broken and festering.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: “My days are swifter than a weaver`s shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: Remember, O God, that my life is but a breath; my eyes will never see happiness again.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: The eye that now sees me will see me no longer; you will look for me, but I will be no more.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so one who goes down to the grave does not return.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: He will never come to his house again; his place will know him no more.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: “Therefore I will not keep silent; I will speak out in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that you put me under guard?

7.speaker: job
7.quote: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,

7.speaker: job
7.quote: even then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,

7.speaker: job
7.quote: so that I prefer strangling and death, rather than this body of mine.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: I despise my life; I would not live forever. Let me alone; my days have no meaning.

7.speaker: job
7.quote: “What is mankind that you make so much of them, that you give them so much attention,

7.speaker: job
7.quote: that you examine them every morning and test them every moment?

7.speaker: job
7.quote: Will you never look away from me, or let me alone even for an instant?

7.speaker: job
7.quote: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, you who see everything we do? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?

7.speaker: job
7.quote: Why do you not pardon my offenses and forgive my sins? For I will soon lie down in the dust; you will search for me, but I will be no more.”

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: “How long will you say such things? Your words are a blustering wind.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: When your children sinned against him, he gave them over to the penalty of their sin.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: But if you will seek God earnestly and plead with the Almighty,

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: if you are pure and upright, even now he will rouse himself on your behalf and restore you to your prosperous state.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: “Ask the former generation and find out what their ancestors learned,

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: for we were born only yesterday and know nothing, and our days on earth are but a shadow.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Will they not instruct you and tell you? Will they not bring forth words from their understanding?

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds thrive without water?

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: While still growing and uncut, they wither more quickly than grass.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so perishes the hope of the godless.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: What they trust in is fragile; what they rely on is a spider`s web.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: They lean on the web, but it gives way; they cling to it, but it does not hold.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: They are like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden;

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: it entwines its roots around a pile of rocks and looks for a place among the stones.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: But when it is torn from its spot, that place disowns it and says, ‘I never saw you.`

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Surely its life withers away, and from the soil other plants grow.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: “Surely God does not reject one who is blameless or strengthen the hands of evildoers.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.

8.speaker: bildad
8.quote: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tents of the wicked will be no more.”

9.speaker: job
9.quote: “Indeed, I know that this is true. But how can mere mortals prove their innocence before God?

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Though they wished to dispute with him, they could not answer him one time out of a thousand.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: His wisdom is profound, his power is vast. Who has resisted him and come out unscathed?

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He moves mountains without their knowing it and overturns them in his anger.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He shakes the earth from its place and makes its pillars tremble.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He speaks to the sun and it does not shine; he seals off the light of the stars.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: When he passes me, I cannot see him; when he goes by, I cannot perceive him.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: If he snatches away, who can stop him? Who can say to him, ‘What are you doing?`

9.speaker: job
9.quote: God does not restrain his anger; even the cohorts of Rahab cowered at his feet.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: “How then can I dispute with him? How can I find words to argue with him?

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Though I were innocent, I could not answer him; I could only plead with my Judge for mercy.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Even if I summoned him and he responded, I do not believe he would give me a hearing.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He would crush me with a storm and multiply my wounds for no reason.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: He would not let me catch my breath but would overwhelm me with misery.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty! And if it is a matter of justice, who can challenge him?

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Even if I were innocent, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would pronounce me guilty.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: “Although I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: It is all the same; that is why I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.`

9.speaker: job
9.quote: When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he blindfolds its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?

9.speaker: job
9.quote: “My days are swifter than a runner; they fly away without a glimpse of joy.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: They skim past like boats of papyrus, like eagles swooping down on their prey.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression, and smile,`

9.speaker: job
9.quote: I still dread all my sufferings, for I know you will not hold me innocent.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Since I am already found guilty, why should I struggle in vain?

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Even if I washed myself with soap and my hands with cleansing powder,

9.speaker: job
9.quote: you would plunge me into a slime pit so that even my clothes would detest me.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: “He is not a mere mortal like me that I might answer him, that we might confront each other in court.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: If only there were someone to mediate between us, someone to bring us together,

9.speaker: job
9.quote: someone to remove God`s rod from me, so that his terror would frighten me no more.

9.speaker: job
9.quote: Then I would speak up without fear of him, but as it now stands with me, I cannot.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: “I loathe my very life; therefore I will give free rein to my complaint and speak out in the bitterness of my soul.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: I say to God: Do not declare me guilty, but tell me what charges you have against me.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: Does it please you to oppress me, to spurn the work of your hands, while you smile on the plans of the wicked?

10.speaker: job
10.quote: Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?

10.speaker: job
10.quote: Are your days like those of a mortal or your years like those of a strong man,

10.speaker: job
10.quote: that you must search out my faults and probe after my sin—

10.speaker: job
10.quote: though you know that I am not guilty and that no one can rescue me from your hand?

10.speaker: job
10.quote: “Your hands shaped me and made me. Will you now turn and destroy me?

10.speaker: job
10.quote: Remember that you molded me like clay. Will you now turn me to dust again?

10.speaker: job
10.quote: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese,

10.speaker: job
10.quote: clothe me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews?

10.speaker: job
10.quote: You gave me life and showed me kindness, and in your providence watched over my spirit.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: “But this is what you concealed in your heart, and I know that this was in your mind:

10.speaker: job
10.quote: If I sinned, you would be watching me and would not let my offense go unpunished.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: If I am guilty—woe to me! Even if I am innocent, I cannot lift my head, for I am full of shame and drowned in my affliction.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: If I hold my head high, you stalk me like a lion and again display your awesome power against me.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: You bring new witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me; your forces come against me wave upon wave.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: “Why then did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye saw me.

10.speaker: job
10.quote: If only I had never come into being, or had been carried straight from the womb to the grave!

10.speaker: job
10.quote: Are not my few days almost over? Turn away from me so I can have a moment`s joy

10.speaker: job
10.quote: before I go to the place of no return, to the land of gloom and utter darkness,

10.speaker: job
10.quote: to the land of deepest night, of utter darkness and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: “Are all these words to go unanswered? Is this talker to be vindicated?

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: Will your idle talk reduce others to silence? Will no one rebuke you when you mock?

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: You say to God, ‘My beliefs are flawless and I am pure in your sight.`

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: Oh, how I wish that God would speak, that he would open his lips against you

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know this: God has even forgotten some of your sin.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: “Can you fathom the mysteries of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: They are higher than the heavens above—what can you do? They are deeper than the depths below—what can you know?

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: “If he comes along and confines you in prison and convenes a court, who can oppose him?

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: Surely he recognizes deceivers; and when he sees evil, does he not take note?

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: But the witless can no more become wise than a wild donkey`s colt can be born human.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: “Yet if you devote your heart to him and stretch out your hands to him,

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: if you put away the sin that is in your hand and allow no evil to dwell in your tent,

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: then, free of fault, you will lift up your face; you will stand firm and without fear.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: You will surely forget your trouble, recalling it only as waters gone by.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: Life will be brighter than noonday, and darkness will become like morning.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: You will be secure, because there is hope; you will look about you and take your rest in safety.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: You will lie down, with no one to make you afraid, and many will court your favor.

11.speaker: zophar
11.quote: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; their hope will become a dying gasp.”

12.speaker: job
12.quote: “Doubtless you are the only people who matter, and wisdom will die with you!

12.speaker: job
12.quote: But I have a mind as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know all these things?

12.speaker: job
12.quote: “I have become a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God and he answered— a mere laughingstock, though righteous and blameless!

12.speaker: job
12.quote: Those who are at ease have contempt for misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: The tents of marauders are undisturbed, and those who provoke God are secure— those God has in his hand.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: “But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you;

12.speaker: job
12.quote: or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the Lord has done this?

12.speaker: job
12.quote: In his hand is the life of every creature and the breath of all mankind.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes food?

12.speaker: job
12.quote: Is not wisdom found among the aged? Does not long life bring understanding?

12.speaker: job
12.quote: “To God belong wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; those he imprisons cannot be released.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: If he holds back the waters, there is drought; if he lets them loose, they devastate the land.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: To him belong strength and insight; both deceived and deceiver are his.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He leads rulers away stripped and makes fools of judges.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He takes off the shackles put on by kings and ties a loincloth around their waist.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows officials long established.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He silences the lips of trusted advisers and takes away the discernment of elders.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He pours contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings utter darkness into the light.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He makes nations great, and destroys them; he enlarges nations, and disperses them.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: He deprives the leaders of the earth of their reason; he makes them wander in a trackless waste.

12.speaker: job
12.quote: They grope in darkness with no light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: “My eyes have seen all this, my ears have heard and understood it.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: But I desire to speak to the Almighty and to argue my case with God.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: You, however, smear me with lies; you are worthless physicians, all of you!

13.speaker: job
13.quote: If only you would be altogether silent! For you, that would be wisdom.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Hear now my argument; listen to the pleas of my lips.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Will you speak wickedly on God`s behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Would it turn out well if he examined you? Could you deceive him as you might deceive a mortal?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: He would surely call you to account if you secretly showed partiality.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Would not his splendor terrify you? Would not the dread of him fall on you?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: “Keep silent and let me speak; then let come to me what may.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Why do I put myself in jeopardy and take my life in my hands?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Though he slay me, yet will I hope in him; I will surely defend my ways to his face.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Indeed, this will turn out for my deliverance, for no godless person would dare come before him!

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Listen carefully to what I say; let my words ring in your ears.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Now that I have prepared my case, I know I will be vindicated.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Can anyone bring charges against me? If so, I will be silent and die.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: “Only grant me these two things, God, and then I will not hide from you:

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Withdraw your hand far from me, and stop frightening me with your terrors.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Then summon me and I will answer, or let me speak, and you reply to me.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: How many wrongs and sins have I committed? Show me my offense and my sin.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: Will you torment a windblown leaf? Will you chase after dry chaff?

13.speaker: job
13.quote: For you write down bitter things against me and make me reap the sins of my youth.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: You fasten my feet in shackles; you keep close watch on all my paths by putting marks on the soles of my feet.

13.speaker: job
13.quote: “So man wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: “Mortals, born of woman, are of few days and full of trouble.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: They spring up like flowers and wither away; like fleeting shadows, they do not endure.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: Do you fix your eye on them? Will you bring them before you for judgment?

14.speaker: job
14.quote: Who can bring what is pure from the impure? No one!

14.speaker: job
14.quote: A person`s days are determined; you have decreed the number of his months and have set limits he cannot exceed.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: So look away from him and let him alone, till he has put in his time like a hired laborer.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: “At least there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will not fail.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: Its roots may grow old in the ground and its stump die in the soil,

14.speaker: job
14.quote: yet at the scent of water it will bud and put forth shoots like a plant.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last and is no more.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: As the water of a lake dries up or a riverbed becomes parched and dry,

14.speaker: job
14.quote: so he lies down and does not rise; till the heavens are no more, people will not awake or be roused from their sleep.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: “If only you would hide me in the grave and conceal me till your anger has passed! If only you would set me a time and then remember me!

14.speaker: job
14.quote: If someone dies, will they live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait for my renewal to come.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: You will call and I will answer you; you will long for the creature your hands have made.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: Surely then you will count my steps but not keep track of my sin.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: My offenses will be sealed up in a bag; you will cover over my sin.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: “But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and as a rock is moved from its place,

14.speaker: job
14.quote: as water wears away stones and torrents wash away the soil, so you destroy a person`s hope.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: You overpower them once for all, and they are gone; you change their countenance and send them away.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: If their children are honored, they do not know it; if their offspring are brought low, they do not see it.

14.speaker: job
14.quote: They feel but the pain of their own bodies and mourn only for themselves.”

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: “Would a wise person answer with empty notions or fill their belly with the hot east wind?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Would they argue with useless words, with speeches that have no value?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: But you even undermine piety and hinder devotion to God.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Your sin prompts your mouth; you adopt the tongue of the crafty.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Your own mouth condemns you, not mine; your own lips testify against you.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: “Are you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Do you listen in on God`s council? Do you have a monopoly on wisdom?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: What do you know that we do not know? What insights do you have that we do not have?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: The gray-haired and the aged are on our side, men even older than your father.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Are God`s consolations not enough for you, words spoken gently to you?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: so that you vent your rage against God and pour out such words from your mouth?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: “What are mortals, that they could be pure, or those born of woman, that they could be righteous?

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: If God places no trust in his holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in his eyes,

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: how much less mortals, who are vile and corrupt, who drink up evil like water!

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: “Listen to me and I will explain to you; let me tell you what I have seen,

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: what the wise have declared, hiding nothing received from their ancestors

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: (to whom alone the land was given when no foreigners moved among them):

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: All his days the wicked man suffers torment, the ruthless man through all the years stored up for him.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Terrifying sounds fill his ears; when all seems well, marauders attack him.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: He despairs of escaping the realm of darkness; he is marked for the sword.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: He wanders about for food like a vulture; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Distress and anguish fill him with terror; troubles overwhelm him, like a king poised to attack,

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: because he shakes his fist at God and vaunts himself against the Almighty,

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: defiantly charging against him with a thick, strong shield.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: “Though his face is covered with fat and his waist bulges with flesh,

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: he will inhabit ruined towns and houses where no one lives, houses crumbling to rubble.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: He will no longer be rich and his wealth will not endure, nor will his possessions spread over the land.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God`s mouth will carry him away.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Let him not deceive himself by trusting what is worthless, for he will get nothing in return.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: Before his time he will wither, and his branches will not flourish.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree shedding its blossoms.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of those who love bribes.

15.speaker: eliphaz
15.quote: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb fashions deceit.”

16.speaker: job
16.quote: “I have heard many things like these; you are miserable comforters, all of you!

16.speaker: job
16.quote: Will your long-winded speeches never end? What ails you that you keep on arguing?

16.speaker: job
16.quote: I also could speak like you, if you were in my place; I could make fine speeches against you and shake my head at you.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: But my mouth would encourage you; comfort from my lips would bring you relief.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: “Yet if I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I refrain, it does not go away.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: Surely, God, you have worn me out; you have devastated my entire household.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: You have shriveled me up—and it has become a witness; my gauntness rises up and testifies against me.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: God assails me and tears me in his anger and gnashes his teeth at me; my opponent fastens on me his piercing eyes.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: People open their mouths to jeer at me; they strike my cheek in scorn and unite together against me.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: God has turned me over to the ungodly and thrown me into the clutches of the wicked.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: All was well with me, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has made me his target;

16.speaker: job
16.quote: his archers surround me. Without pity, he pierces my kidneys and spills my gall on the ground.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: Again and again he bursts upon me; he rushes at me like a warrior.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: “I have sewed sackcloth over my skin and buried my brow in the dust.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: My face is red with weeping, dark shadows ring my eyes;

16.speaker: job
16.quote: yet my hands have been free of violence and my prayer is pure.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: “Earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry never be laid to rest!

16.speaker: job
16.quote: Even now my witness is in heaven; my advocate is on high.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: My intercessor is my friend as my eyes pour out tears to God;

16.speaker: job
16.quote: on behalf of a man he pleads with God as one pleads for a friend.

16.speaker: job
16.quote: “Only a few years will pass before I take the path of no return.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: My spirit is broken, my days are cut short, the grave awaits me.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: Surely mockers surround me; my eyes must dwell on their hostility.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: “Give me, O God, the pledge you demand. Who else will put up security for me?

17.speaker: job
17.quote: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: If anyone denounces their friends for reward, the eyes of their children will fail.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: “God has made me a byword to everyone, a man in whose face people spit.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: My eyes have grown dim with grief; my whole frame is but a shadow.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: The upright are appalled at this; the innocent are aroused against the ungodly.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: Nevertheless, the righteous will hold to their ways, and those with clean hands will grow stronger.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: “But come on, all of you, try again! I will not find a wise man among you.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: My days have passed, my plans are shattered. Yet the desires of my heart

17.speaker: job
17.quote: turn night into day; in the face of the darkness light is near.

17.speaker: job
17.quote: If the only home I hope for is the grave, if I spread out my bed in the realm of darkness,

17.speaker: job
17.quote: if I say to corruption, ‘You are my father,` and to the worm, ‘My mother` or ‘My sister,`

17.speaker: job
17.quote: where then is my hope— who can see any hope for me?

17.speaker: job
17.quote: Will it go down to the gates of death? Will we descend together into the dust?”

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: “When will you end these speeches? Be sensible, and then we can talk.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: Why are we regarded as cattle and considered stupid in your sight?

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: You who tear yourself to pieces in your anger, is the earth to be abandoned for your sake? Or must the rocks be moved from their place?

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: “The lamp of a wicked man is snuffed out; the flame of his fire stops burning.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: The light in his tent becomes dark; the lamp beside him goes out.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: The vigor of his step is weakened; his own schemes throw him down.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: His feet thrust him into a net; he wanders into its mesh.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare holds him fast.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: A noose is hidden for him on the ground; a trap lies in his path.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: Terrors startle him on every side and dog his every step.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: Calamity is hungry for him; disaster is ready for him when he falls.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: It eats away parts of his skin; death`s firstborn devours his limbs.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: He is torn from the security of his tent and marched off to the king of terrors.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: His roots dry up below and his branches wither above.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: The memory of him perishes from the earth; he has no name in the land.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: He is driven from light into the realm of darkness and is banished from the world.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: He has no offspring or descendants among his people, no survivor where once he lived.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: People of the west are appalled at his fate; those of the east are seized with horror.

18.speaker: bildad
18.quote: Surely such is the dwelling of an evil man; such is the place of one who does not know God.”

19.speaker: job
19.quote: “How long will you torment me and crush me with words?

19.speaker: job
19.quote: Ten times now you have reproached me; shamelessly you attack me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: If it is true that I have gone astray, my error remains my concern alone.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my humiliation against me,

19.speaker: job
19.quote: then know that God has wronged me and drawn his net around me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: “Though I cry, ‘Violence!` I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; he has shrouded my paths in darkness.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: He tears me down on every side till I am gone; he uproots my hope like a tree.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: His anger burns against me; he counts me among his enemies.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: His troops advance in force; they build a siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: “He has alienated my family from me; my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: My relatives have gone away; my closest friends have forgotten me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: My guests and my female servants count me a foreigner; they look on me as on a stranger.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: I summon my servant, but he does not answer, though I beg him with my own mouth.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: My breath is offensive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own family.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: Even the little boys scorn me; when I appear, they ridicule me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: All my intimate friends detest me; those I love have turned against me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: I am nothing but skin and bones; I have escaped only by the skin of my teeth.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: “Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: Why do you pursue me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?

19.speaker: job
19.quote: “Oh, that my words were recorded, that they were written on a scroll,

19.speaker: job
19.quote: that they were inscribed with an iron tool on lead, or engraved in rock forever!

19.speaker: job
19.quote: I know that my redeemer lives, and that in the end he will stand on the earth.

19.speaker: job
19.quote: And after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God;

19.speaker: job
19.quote: I myself will see him with my own eyes—I, and not another. How my heart yearns within me!

19.speaker: job
19.quote: “If you say, ‘How we will hound him, since the root of the trouble lies in him,`

19.speaker: job
19.quote: you should fear the sword yourselves; for wrath will bring punishment by the sword, and then you will know that there is judgment.”

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: “My troubled thoughts prompt me to answer because I am greatly disturbed.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: I hear a rebuke that dishonors me, and my understanding inspires me to reply.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: “Surely you know how it has been from of old, ever since mankind was placed on the earth,

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: that the mirth of the wicked is brief, the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: Though the pride of the godless person reaches to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?`

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: Like a dream he flies away, no more to be found, banished like a vision of the night.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: The eye that saw him will not see him again; his place will look on him no more.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: His children must make amends to the poor; his own hands must give back his wealth.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie with him in the dust.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: “Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: though he cannot bear to let it go and lets it linger in his mouth,

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: yet his food will turn sour in his stomach; it will become the venom of serpents within him.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: He will spit out the riches he swallowed; God will make his stomach vomit them up.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: He will suck the poison of serpents; the fangs of an adder will kill him.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: What he toiled for he must give back uneaten; he will not enjoy the profit from his trading.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: For he has oppressed the poor and left them destitute; he has seized houses he did not build.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: “Surely he will have no respite from his craving; he cannot save himself by his treasure.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: Nothing is left for him to devour; his prosperity will not endure.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: In the midst of his plenty, distress will overtake him; the full force of misery will come upon him.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: When he has filled his belly, God will vent his burning anger against him and rain down his blows on him.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow pierces him.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: He pulls it out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver. Terrors will come over him;

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: total darkness lies in wait for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: The heavens will expose his guilt; the earth will rise up against him.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: A flood will carry off his house, rushing waters on the day of God`s wrath.

20.speaker: zophar
20.quote: Such is the fate God allots the wicked, the heritage appointed for them by God.”

21.speaker: job
21.quote: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be the consolation you give me.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, mock on.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: “Is my complaint directed to a human being? Why should I not be impatient?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Look at me and be appalled; clap your hand over your mouth.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: When I think about this, I am terrified; trembling seizes my body.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: They see their children established around them, their offspring before their eyes.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Their homes are safe and free from fear; the rod of God is not on them.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Their bulls never fail to breed; their cows calve and do not miscarry.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: They send forth their children as a flock; their little ones dance about.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: They sing to the music of timbrel and lyre; they make merry to the sound of the pipe.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: They spend their years in prosperity and go down to the grave in peace.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Yet they say to God, ‘Leave us alone! We have no desire to know your ways.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?`

21.speaker: job
21.quote: But their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stand aloof from the plans of the wicked.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: “Yet how often is the lamp of the wicked snuffed out? How often does calamity come upon them, the fate God allots in his anger?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a gale?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: It is said, ‘God stores up the punishment of the wicked for their children.` Let him repay the wicked, so that they themselves will experience it!

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Let their own eyes see their destruction; let them drink the cup of the wrath of the Almighty.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: For what do they care about the families they leave behind when their allotted months come to an end?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: “Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since he judges even the highest?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: One person dies in full vigor, completely secure and at ease,

21.speaker: job
21.quote: well nourished in body, bones rich with marrow.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Another dies in bitterness of soul, never having enjoyed anything good.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Side by side they lie in the dust, and worms cover them both.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: “I know full well what you are thinking, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: You say, ‘Where now is the house of the great, the tents where the wicked lived?`

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Have you never questioned those who travel? Have you paid no regard to their accounts—

21.speaker: job
21.quote: that the wicked are spared from the day of calamity, that they are delivered from the day of wrath?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: Who denounces their conduct to their face? Who repays them for what they have done?

21.speaker: job
21.quote: They are carried to the grave, and watch is kept over their tombs.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: The soil in the valley is sweet to them; everyone follows after them, and a countless throng goes before them.

21.speaker: job
21.quote: “So how can you console me with your nonsense? Nothing is left of your answers but falsehood!”

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: “Can a man be of benefit to God? Can even a wise person benefit him?

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: What pleasure would it give the Almighty if you were righteous? What would he gain if your ways were blameless?

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: “Is it for your piety that he rebukes you and brings charges against you?

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your sins endless?

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: You demanded security from your relatives for no reason; you stripped people of their clothing, leaving them naked.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: You gave no water to the weary and you withheld food from the hungry,

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: though you were a powerful man, owning land— an honored man, living on it.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: And you sent widows away empty-handed and broke the strength of the fatherless.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: That is why snares are all around you, why sudden peril terrifies you,

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: why it is so dark you cannot see, and why a flood of water covers you.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: “Is not God in the heights of heaven? And see how lofty are the highest stars!

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Yet you say, ‘What does God know? Does he judge through such darkness?

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Thick clouds veil him, so he does not see us as he goes about in the vaulted heavens.`

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Will you keep to the old path that the wicked have trod?

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: They were carried off before their time, their foundations washed away by a flood.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: They said to God, ‘Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?`

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things, so I stand aloof from the plans of the wicked.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: The righteous see their ruin and rejoice; the innocent mock them, saying,

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire devours their wealth.`

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: “Submit to God and be at peace with him; in this way prosperity will come to you.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Accept instruction from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored: If you remove wickedness far from your tent

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: and assign your nuggets to the dust, your gold of Ophir to the rocks in the ravines,

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: then the Almighty will be your gold, the choicest silver for you.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: Surely then you will find delight in the Almighty and will lift up your face to God.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: What you decide on will be done, and light will shine on your ways.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: When people are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!` then he will save the downcast.

22.speaker: eliphaz
22.quote: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, who will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

23.speaker: job
23.quote: “Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: If only I knew where to find him; if only I could go to his dwelling!

23.speaker: job
23.quote: I would state my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: I would find out what he would answer me, and consider what he would say to me.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: Would he vigorously oppose me? No, he would not press charges against me.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: There the upright can establish their innocence before him, and there I would be delivered forever from my judge.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: “But if I go to the east, he is not there; if I go to the west, I do not find him.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: When he is at work in the north, I do not see him; when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I will come forth as gold.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: My feet have closely followed his steps; I have kept to his way without turning aside.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: I have not departed from the commands of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: “But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? He does whatever he pleases.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: He carries out his decree against me, and many such plans he still has in store.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: That is why I am terrified before him; when I think of all this, I fear him.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.

23.speaker: job
23.quote: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: “Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why must those who know him look in vain for such days?

24.speaker: job
24.quote: There are those who move boundary stones; they pasture flocks they have stolen.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: They drive away the orphan`s donkey and take the widow`s ox in pledge.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: They thrust the needy from the path and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go about their labor of foraging food; the wasteland provides food for their children.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: They gather fodder in the fields and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: Lacking clothes, they spend the night naked; they have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: They are drenched by mountain rains and hug the rocks for lack of shelter.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: The fatherless child is snatched from the breast; the infant of the poor is seized for a debt.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: Lacking clothes, they go about naked; they carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: They crush olives among the terraces; they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: The groans of the dying rise from the city, and the souls of the wounded cry out for help. But God charges no one with wrongdoing.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: “There are those who rebel against the light, who do not know its ways or stay in its paths.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises up, kills the poor and needy, and in the night steals forth like a thief.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk; he thinks, ‘No eye will see me,` and he keeps his face concealed.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: In the dark, thieves break into houses, but by day they shut themselves in; they want nothing to do with the light.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: For all of them, midnight is their morning; they make friends with the terrors of darkness.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: “Yet they are foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one goes to the vineyards.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: As heat and drought snatch away the melted snow, so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: The womb forgets them, the worm feasts on them; the wicked are no longer remembered but are broken like a tree.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: They prey on the barren and childless woman, and to the widow they show no kindness.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: But God drags away the mighty by his power; though they become established, they have no assurance of life.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: He may let them rest in a feeling of security, but his eyes are on their ways.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: For a little while they are exalted, and then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

24.speaker: job
24.quote: “If this is not so, who can prove me false and reduce my words to nothing?”

25.speaker: bildad
25.quote: “Dominion and awe belong to God; he establishes order in the heights of heaven.

25.speaker: bildad
25.quote: Can his forces be numbered? On whom does his light not rise?

25.speaker: bildad
25.quote: How then can a mortal be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

25.speaker: bildad
25.quote: If even the moon is not bright and the stars are not pure in his eyes,

25.speaker: bildad
25.quote: how much less a mortal, who is but a maggot— a human being, who is only a worm!”

26.speaker: job
26.quote: “How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm that is feeble!

26.speaker: job
26.quote: What advice you have offered to one without wisdom! And what great insight you have displayed!

26.speaker: job
26.quote: Who has helped you utter these words? And whose spirit spoke from your mouth?

26.speaker: job
26.quote: “The dead are in deep anguish, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: The realm of the dead is naked before God; Destruction lies uncovered.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: He spreads out the northern skies over empty space; he suspends the earth over nothing.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: He wraps up the waters in his clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their weight.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading his clouds over it.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: He marks out the horizon on the face of the waters for a boundary between light and darkness.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: The pillars of the heavens quake, aghast at his rebuke.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: By his power he churned up the sea; by his wisdom he cut Rahab to pieces.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: By his breath the skies became fair; his hand pierced the gliding serpent.

26.speaker: job
26.quote: And these are but the outer fringe of his works; how faint the whisper we hear of him! Who then can understand the thunder of his power?”

27.speaker: job
27.quote: And Job continued his discourse:

27.speaker: job
27.quote: “As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice, the Almighty, who has made my life bitter,

27.speaker: job
27.quote: as long as I have life within me, the breath of God in my nostrils,

27.speaker: job
27.quote: my lips will not say anything wicked, and my tongue will not utter lies.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: I will never admit you are in the right; till I die, I will not deny my integrity.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: I will maintain my innocence and never let go of it; my conscience will not reproach me as long as I live.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: “May my enemy be like the wicked, my adversary like the unjust!

27.speaker: job
27.quote: For what hope have the godless when they are cut off, when God takes away their life?

27.speaker: job
27.quote: Does God listen to their cry when distress comes upon them?

27.speaker: job
27.quote: Will they find delight in the Almighty? Will they call on God at all times?

27.speaker: job
27.quote: “I will teach you about the power of God; the ways of the Almighty I will not conceal.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: You have all seen this yourselves. Why then this meaningless talk?

27.speaker: job
27.quote: “Here is the fate God allots to the wicked, the heritage a ruthless man receives from the Almighty:

27.speaker: job
27.quote: However many his children, their fate is the sword; his offspring will never have enough to eat.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: The plague will bury those who survive him, and their widows will not weep for them.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: Though he heaps up silver like dust and clothes like piles of clay,

27.speaker: job
27.quote: what he lays up the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: The house he builds is like a moth`s cocoon, like a hut made by a watchman.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest snatches him away in the night.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: The east wind carries him off, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.

27.speaker: job
27.quote: It claps its hands in derision and hisses him out of his place.”

28.speaker: job
28.quote: There is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Mortals put an end to the darkness; they search out the farthest recesses for ore in the blackest darkness.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Far from human dwellings they cut a shaft, in places untouched by human feet; far from other people they dangle and sway.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: The earth, from which food comes, is transformed below as by fire;

28.speaker: job
28.quote: lapis lazuli comes from its rocks, and its dust contains nuggets of gold.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: No bird of prey knows that hidden path, no falcon`s eye has seen it.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Proud beasts do not set foot on it, and no lion prowls there.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: People assault the flinty rock with their hands and lay bare the roots of the mountains.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: They tunnel through the rock; their eyes see all its treasures.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: They search the sources of the rivers and bring hidden things to light.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: But where can wisdom be found? Where does understanding dwell?

28.speaker: job
28.quote: No mortal comprehends its worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: The deep says, “It is not in me”; the sea says, “It is not with me.”

28.speaker: job
28.quote: It cannot be bought with the finest gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: It cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or lapis lazuli.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Neither gold nor crystal can compare with it, nor can it be had for jewels of gold.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Coral and jasper are not worthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: The topaz of Cush cannot compare with it; it cannot be bought with pure gold.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Where then does wisdom come from? Where does understanding dwell?

28.speaker: job
28.quote: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds in the sky.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: Destruction and Death say, “Only a rumor of it has reached our ears.”

28.speaker: job
28.quote: God understands the way to it and he alone knows where it dwells,

28.speaker: job
28.quote: for he views the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: When he established the force of the wind and measured out the waters,

28.speaker: job
28.quote: when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderstorm,

28.speaker: job
28.quote: then he looked at wisdom and appraised it; he confirmed it and tested it.

28.speaker: job
28.quote: And he said to the human race, “The fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and to shun evil is understanding.”

29.speaker: job
29.quote: Job continued his discourse:

29.speaker: job
29.quote: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,

29.speaker: job
29.quote: when his lamp shone on my head and by his light I walked through darkness!

29.speaker: job
29.quote: Oh, for the days when I was in my prime, when God`s intimate friendship blessed my house,

29.speaker: job
29.quote: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,

29.speaker: job
29.quote: when my path was drenched with cream and the rock poured out for me streams of olive oil.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: “When I went to the gate of the city and took my seat in the public square,

29.speaker: job
29.quote: the young men saw me and stepped aside and the old men rose to their feet;

29.speaker: job
29.quote: the chief men refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands;

29.speaker: job
29.quote: the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: Whoever heard me spoke well of me, and those who saw me commended me,

29.speaker: job
29.quote: because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had none to assist them.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: The one who was dying blessed me; I made the widow`s heart sing.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: I put on righteousness as my clothing; justice was my robe and my turban.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: I was a father to the needy; I took up the case of the stranger.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the victims from their teeth.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: “I thought, ‘I will die in my own house, my days as numerous as the grains of sand.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: My roots will reach to the water, and the dew will lie all night on my branches.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: My glory will not fade; the bow will be ever new in my hand.`

29.speaker: job
29.quote: “People listened to me expectantly, waiting in silence for my counsel.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: After I had spoken, they spoke no more; my words fell gently on their ears.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: They waited for me as for showers and drank in my words as the spring rain.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: When I smiled at them, they scarcely believed it; the light of my face was precious to them.

29.speaker: job
29.quote: I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I dwelt as a king among his troops; I was like one who comforts mourners.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: “But now they mock me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with my sheep dogs.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Of what use was the strength of their hands to me, since their vigor had gone from them?

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Haggard from want and hunger, they roamed the parched land in desolate wastelands at night.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: In the brush they gathered salt herbs, and their food was the root of the broom bush.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: They were banished from human society, shouted at as if they were thieves.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: They were forced to live in the dry stream beds, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: They brayed among the bushes and huddled in the undergrowth.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: A base and nameless brood, they were driven out of the land.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: “And now those young men mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: They detest me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Now that God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they throw off restraint in my presence.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: On my right the tribe attacks; they lay snares for my feet, they build their siege ramps against me.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: They break up my road; they succeed in destroying me. ‘No one can help him,` they say.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: They advance as through a gaping breach; amid the ruins they come rolling in.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Terrors overwhelm me; my dignity is driven away as by the wind, my safety vanishes like a cloud.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: “And now my life ebbs away; days of suffering grip me.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Night pierces my bones; my gnawing pains never rest.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: In his great power God becomes like clothing to me; he binds me like the neck of my garment.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: He throws me into the mud, and I am reduced to dust and ashes.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: “I cry out to you, God, but you do not answer; I stand up, but you merely look at me.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: You turn on me ruthlessly; with the might of your hand you attack me.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: You snatch me up and drive me before the wind; you toss me about in the storm.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: I know you will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: “Surely no one lays a hand on a broken man when he cries for help in his distress.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has not my soul grieved for the poor?

30.speaker: job
30.quote: Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, then came darkness.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: The churning inside me never stops; days of suffering confront me.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of owls.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: My skin grows black and peels; my body burns with fever.

30.speaker: job
30.quote: My lyre is tuned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of wailing.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a young woman.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: For what is our lot from God above, our heritage from the Almighty on high?

31.speaker: job
31.quote: Is it not ruin for the wicked, disaster for those who do wrong?

31.speaker: job
31.quote: Does he not see my ways and count my every step?

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “If I have walked with falsehood or my foot has hurried after deceit—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: let God weigh me in honest scales and he will know that I am blameless—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has been led by my eyes, or if my hands have been defiled,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: then may others eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if I have lurked at my neighbor`s door,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: then may my wife grind another man`s grain, and may other men sleep with her.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: For that would have been wicked, a sin to be judged.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: It is a fire that burns to Destruction; it would have uprooted my harvest.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “If I have denied justice to any of my servants, whether male or female, when they had a grievance against me,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: what will I do when God confronts me? What will I answer when called to account?

31.speaker: job
31.quote: Did not he who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same one form us both within our mothers?

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “If I have denied the desires of the poor or let the eyes of the widow grow weary,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have kept my bread to myself, not sharing it with the fatherless—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: but from my youth I reared them as a father would, and from my birth I guided the widow—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or the needy without garments,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: and their hearts did not bless me for warming them with the fleece from my sheep,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, knowing that I had influence in court,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: then let my arm fall from the shoulder, let it be broken off at the joint.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: For I dreaded destruction from God, and for fear of his splendor I could not do such things.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “If I have put my trust in gold or said to pure gold, ‘You are my security,`

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have rejoiced over my great wealth, the fortune my hands had gained,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have regarded the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand offered them a kiss of homage,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: then these also would be sins to be judged, for I would have been unfaithful to God on high.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “If I have rejoiced at my enemy`s misfortune or gloated over the trouble that came to him—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by invoking a curse against their life—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if those of my household have never said, ‘Who has not been filled with Job`s meat?`—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: but no stranger had to spend the night in the street, for my door was always open to the traveler—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have concealed my sin as people do, by hiding my guilt in my heart

31.speaker: job
31.quote: because I so feared the crowd and so dreaded the contempt of the clans that I kept silent and would not go outside—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: (“Oh, that I had someone to hear me! I sign now my defense—let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser put his indictment in writing.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: Surely I would wear it on my shoulder, I would put it on like a crown.

31.speaker: job
31.quote: I would give him an account of my every step; I would present it to him as to a ruler.)—

31.speaker: job
31.quote: “if my land cries out against me and all its furrows are wet with tears,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: if I have devoured its yield without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,

31.speaker: job
31.quote: then let briers come up instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: But Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became very angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God.

32.speaker: elihu
