32.quote: He was also angry with the three friends, because they had found no way to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: Now Elihu had waited before speaking to Job because they were older than he.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: But when he saw that the three men had nothing more to say, his anger was aroused.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: So Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite said: “I am young in years, and you are old; that is why I was fearful, not daring to tell you what I know.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: I thought, ‘Age should speak; advanced years should teach wisdom.`

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: It is not only the old who are wise, not only the aged who understand what is right.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: “Therefore I say: Listen to me; I too will tell you what I know.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: I waited while you spoke, I listened to your reasoning; while you were searching for words,

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: I gave you my full attention. But not one of you has proved Job wrong; none of you has answered his arguments.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not a man, refute him.`

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: But Job has not marshaled his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: “They are dismayed and have no more to say; words have failed them.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand there with no reply?

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: I too will have my say; I too will tell what I know.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: For I am full of words, and the spirit within me compels me;

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: inside I am like bottled-up wine, like new wineskins ready to burst.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and reply.

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: I will show no partiality, nor will I flatter anyone;

32.speaker: elihu
32.quote: for if I were skilled in flattery, my Maker would soon take me away.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: “But now, Job, listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: I am about to open my mouth; my words are on the tip of my tongue.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: My words come from an upright heart; my lips sincerely speak what I know.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: The Spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: Answer me then, if you can; stand up and argue your case before me.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: I am the same as you in God`s sight; I too am a piece of clay.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: No fear of me should alarm you, nor should my hand be heavy on you.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: “But you have said in my hearing— I heard the very words—

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: ‘I am pure, I have done no wrong; I am clean and free from sin.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: Yet God has found fault with me; he considers me his enemy.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: He fastens my feet in shackles; he keeps close watch on all my paths.`

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: “But I tell you, in this you are not right, for God is greater than any mortal.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: Why do you complain to him that he responds to no one`s words?

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: For God does speak—now one way, now another— though no one perceives it.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber in their beds,

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: he may speak in their ears and terrify them with warnings,

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: to turn them from wrongdoing and keep them from pride,

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: to preserve them from the pit, their lives from perishing by the sword.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: “Or someone may be chastened on a bed of pain with constant distress in their bones,

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: so that their body finds food repulsive and their soul loathes the choicest meal.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: Their flesh wastes away to nothing, and their bones, once hidden, now stick out.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: They draw near to the pit, and their life to the messengers of death.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: Yet if there is an angel at their side, a messenger, one out of a thousand, sent to tell them how to be upright,

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: and he is gracious to that person and says to God, ‘Spare them from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom for them—

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: let their flesh be renewed like a child`s; let them be restored as in the days of their youth`—

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: then that person can pray to God and find favor with him, they will see God`s face and shout for joy; he will restore them to full well-being.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: And they will go to others and say, ‘I have sinned, I have perverted what is right, but I did not get what I deserved.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: God has delivered me from going down to the pit, and I shall live to enjoy the light of life.`

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: “God does all these things to a person— twice, even three times—

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: to turn them back from the pit, that the light of life may shine on them.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: “Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: If you have anything to say, answer me; speak up, for I want to vindicate you.

33.speaker: elihu
33.quote: But if not, then listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Then Elihu said:

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you men of learning.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: For the ear tests words as the tongue tastes food.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Let us discern for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “Job says, ‘I am innocent, but God denies me justice.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Although I am right, I am considered a liar; although I am guiltless, his arrow inflicts an incurable wound.`

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Is there anyone like Job, who drinks scorn like water?

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: He keeps company with evildoers; he associates with the wicked.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: For he says, ‘There is no profit in trying to please God.`

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “So listen to me, you men of understanding. Far be it from God to do evil, from the Almighty to do wrong.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: He repays everyone for what they have done; he brings on them what their conduct deserves.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: It is unthinkable that God would do wrong, that the Almighty would pervert justice.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Who appointed him over the earth? Who put him in charge of the whole world?

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: If it were his intention and he withdrew his spirit and breath,

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: all humanity would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Can someone who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One?

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Is he not the One who says to kings, ‘You are worthless,` and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,`

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: who shows no partiality to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands?

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and they pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “His eyes are on the ways of mortals; he sees their every step.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: There is no deep shadow, no utter darkness, where evildoers can hide.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: God has no need to examine people further, that they should come before him for judgment.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Without inquiry he shatters the mighty and sets up others in their place.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Because he takes note of their deeds, he overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: He punishes them for their wickedness where everyone can see them,

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: because they turned from following him and had no regard for any of his ways.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: They caused the cry of the poor to come before him, so that he heard the cry of the needy.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: But if he remains silent, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he is over individual and nation alike,

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: to keep the godless from ruling, from laying snares for the people.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “Suppose someone says to God, ‘I am guilty but will offend no more.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do so again.`

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Should God then reward you on your terms, when you refuse to repent? You must decide, not I; so tell me what you know.

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: “Men of understanding declare, wise men who hear me say to me,

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.`

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: Oh, that Job might be tested to the utmost for answering like a wicked man!

34.speaker: elihu
34.quote: To his sin he adds rebellion; scornfully he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am in the right, not God.`

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: Yet you ask him, ‘What profit is it to me, and what do I gain by not sinning?`

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: “I would like to reply to you and to your friends with you.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds so high above you.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: If you sin, how does that affect him? If your sins are many, what does that do to him?

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: If you are righteous, what do you give to him, or what does he receive from your hand?

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: Your wickedness only affects humans like yourself, and your righteousness only other people.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: “People cry out under a load of oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the powerful.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: who teaches us more than he teaches the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds in the sky?`

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: He does not answer when people cry out because of the arrogance of the wicked.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: Indeed, God does not listen to their empty plea; the Almighty pays no attention to it.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: How much less, then, will he listen when you say that you do not see him, that your case is before him and you must wait for him,

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: and further, that his anger never punishes and he does not take the least notice of wickedness.

35.speaker: elihu
35.quote: So Job opens his mouth with empty talk; without knowledge he multiplies words.”

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: “Bear with me a little longer and I will show you that there is more to be said in God`s behalf.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: I get my knowledge from afar; I will ascribe justice to my Maker.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Be assured that my words are not false; one who has perfect knowledge is with you.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: “God is mighty, but despises no one; he is mighty, and firm in his purpose.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: He does not keep the wicked alive but gives the afflicted their rights.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: He does not take his eyes off the righteous; he enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: But if people are bound in chains, held fast by cords of affliction,

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: he tells them what they have done— that they have sinned arrogantly.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: He makes them listen to correction and commands them to repent of their evil.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: If they obey and serve him, they will spend the rest of their days in prosperity and their years in contentment.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: But if they do not listen, they will perish by the sword and die without knowledge.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: “The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when he fetters them, they do not cry for help.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: They die in their youth, among male prostitutes of the shrines.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: But those who suffer he delivers in their suffering; he speaks to them in their affliction.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: “He is wooing you from the jaws of distress to a spacious place free from restriction, to the comfort of your table laden with choice food.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have taken hold of you.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Be careful that no one entices you by riches; do not let a large bribe turn you aside.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Would your wealth or even all your mighty efforts sustain you so you would not be in distress?

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Do not long for the night, to drag people away from their homes.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Beware of turning to evil, which you seem to prefer to affliction.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: “God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Who has prescribed his ways for him, or said to him, ‘You have done wrong`?

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Remember to extol his work, which people have praised in song.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: All humanity has seen it; mortals gaze on it from afar.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: How great is God—beyond our understanding! The number of his years is past finding out.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: “He draws up the drops of water, which distill as rain to the streams;

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: the clouds pour down their moisture and abundant showers fall on mankind.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: Who can understand how he spreads out the clouds, how he thunders from his pavilion?

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: See how he scatters his lightning about him, bathing the depths of the sea.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: This is the way he governs the nations and provides food in abundance.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: He fills his hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.

36.speaker: elihu
36.quote: His thunder announces the coming storm; even the cattle make known its approach.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: “At this my heart pounds and leaps from its place.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Listen! Listen to the roar of his voice, to the rumbling that comes from his mouth.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: He unleashes his lightning beneath the whole heaven and sends it to the ends of the earth.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: After that comes the sound of his roar; he thunders with his majestic voice. When his voice resounds, he holds nothing back.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: God`s voice thunders in marvelous ways; he does great things beyond our understanding.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,` and to the rain shower, ‘Be a mighty downpour.`

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: So that everyone he has made may know his work, he stops all people from their labor.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: The animals take cover; they remain in their dens.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: The tempest comes out from its chamber, the cold from the driving winds.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: The breath of God produces ice, and the broad waters become frozen.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: He loads the clouds with moisture; he scatters his lightning through them.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: At his direction they swirl around over the face of the whole earth to do whatever he commands them.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: He brings the clouds to punish people, or to water his earth and show his love.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: “Listen to this, Job; stop and consider God`s wonders.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Do you know how God controls the clouds and makes his lightning flash?

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Do you know how the clouds hang poised, those wonders of him who has perfect knowledge?

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: You who swelter in your clothes when the land lies hushed under the south wind,

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: can you join him in spreading out the skies, hard as a mirror of cast bronze?

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: “Tell us what we should say to him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Now no one can look at the sun, bright as it is in the skies after the wind has swept them clean.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Out of the north he comes in golden splendor; God comes in awesome majesty.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: The Almighty is beyond our reach and exalted in power; in his justice and great righteousness, he does not oppress.

37.speaker: elihu
37.quote: Therefore, people revere him, for does he not have regard for all the wise in heart?”

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Who is this that obscures my plans with words without knowledge?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me.

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Where were you when I laid the earth`s foundation? Tell me, if you understand.

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Who marked off its dimensions? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: On what were its footings set, or who laid its cornerstone—

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Who shut up the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: when I made the clouds its garment and wrapped it in thick darkness,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: when I fixed limits for it and set its doors and bars in place,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: when I said, ‘This far you may come and no farther; here is where your proud waves halt`?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Have you ever given orders to the morning, or shown the dawn its place,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: that it might take the earth by the edges and shake the wicked out of it?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its features stand out like those of a garment.

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: The wicked are denied their light, and their upraised arm is broken.

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Have you journeyed to the springs of the sea or walked in the recesses of the deep?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Have you comprehended the vast expanses of the earth? Tell me, if you know all this.

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “What is the way to the abode of light? And where does darkness reside?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Can you take them to their places? Do you know the paths to their dwellings?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Surely you know, for you were already born! You have lived so many years!

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Have you entered the storehouses of the snow or seen the storehouses of the hail,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: which I reserve for times of trouble, for days of war and battle?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: What is the way to the place where the lightning is dispersed, or the place where the east winds are scattered over the earth?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Who cuts a channel for the torrents of rain, and a path for the thunderstorm,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: to water a land where no one lives, an uninhabited desert,

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: to satisfy a desolate wasteland and make it sprout with grass?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Does the rain have a father? Who fathers the drops of dew?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: From whose womb comes the ice? Who gives birth to the frost from the heavens

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: when the waters become hard as stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades? Can you loosen Orion`s belt?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear with its cubs?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set up God`s dominion over the earth?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Can you raise your voice to the clouds and cover yourself with a flood of water?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Do you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are`?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Who gives the ibis wisdom or gives the rooster understanding?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of the heavens

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: when the dust becomes hard and the clods of earth stick together?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: “Do you hunt the prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of the lions

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in a thicket?

38.speaker: the-lord
38.quote: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God and wander about for lack of food?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: “Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears her fawn?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Do you count the months till they bear? Do you know the time they give birth?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: They crouch down and bring forth their young; their labor pains are ended.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Their young thrive and grow strong in the wilds; they leave and do not return.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: “Who let the wild donkey go free? Who untied its ropes?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: I gave it the wasteland as its home, the salt flats as its habitat.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: It laughs at the commotion in the town; it does not hear a driver`s shout.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: It ranges the hills for its pasture and searches for any green thing.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: “Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will it stay by your manger at night?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Can you hold it to the furrow with a harness? Will it till the valleys behind you?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Will you rely on it for its great strength? Will you leave your heavy work to it?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Can you trust it to haul in your grain and bring it to your threshing floor?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: “The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, though they cannot compare with the wings and feathers of the stork.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: She lays her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand,

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: unmindful that a foot may crush them, that some wild animal may trample them.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers; she cares not that her labor was in vain,

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: for God did not endow her with wisdom or give her a share of good sense.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Yet when she spreads her feathers to run, she laughs at horse and rider.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: “Do you give the horse its strength or clothe its neck with a flowing mane?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Do you make it leap like a locust, striking terror with its proud snorting?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: It paws fiercely, rejoicing in its strength, and charges into the fray.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: It laughs at fear, afraid of nothing; it does not shy away from the sword.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: The quiver rattles against its side, along with the flashing spear and lance.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: In frenzied excitement it eats up the ground; it cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: At the blast of the trumpet it snorts, ‘Aha!` It catches the scent of battle from afar, the shout of commanders and the battle cry.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: “Does the hawk take flight by your wisdom and spread its wings toward the south?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest on high?

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: It dwells on a cliff and stays there at night; a rocky crag is its stronghold.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: From there it looks for food; its eyes detect it from afar.

39.speaker: the-lord
39.quote: Its young ones feast on blood, and where the slain are, there it is.”

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: The Lord said to Job:

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: “Will the one who contends with the Almighty correct him? Let him who accuses God answer him!”

40.speaker: job
40.quote: “I am unworthy—how can I reply to you? I put my hand over my mouth.

40.speaker: job
40.quote: I spoke once, but I have no answer— twice, but I will say no more.”

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: “Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: “Would you discredit my justice? Would you condemn me to justify yourself?

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Do you have an arm like God`s, and can your voice thunder like his?

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Then adorn yourself with glory and splendor, and clothe yourself in honor and majesty.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Unleash the fury of your wrath, look at all who are proud and bring them low,

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: look at all who are proud and humble them, crush the wicked where they stand.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Bury them all in the dust together; shroud their faces in the grave.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Then I myself will admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: “Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you and which feeds on grass like an ox.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: What strength it has in its loins, what power in the muscles of its belly!

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Its tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of its thighs are close-knit.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Its bones are tubes of bronze, its limbs like rods of iron.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: It ranks first among the works of God, yet its Maker can approach it with his sword.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: The hills bring it their produce, and all the wild animals play nearby.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Under the lotus plants it lies, hidden among the reeds in the marsh.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: The lotuses conceal it in their shadow; the poplars by the stream surround it.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: A raging river does not alarm it; it is secure, though the Jordan should surge against its mouth.

40.speaker: the-lord
40.quote: Can anyone capture it by the eyes, or trap it and pierce its nose?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook or tie down its tongue with a rope?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Can you put a cord through its nose or pierce its jaw with a hook?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Will it keep begging you for mercy? Will it speak to you with gentle words?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Will it make an agreement with you for you to take it as your slave for life?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Can you make a pet of it like a bird or put it on a leash for the young women in your house?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Will traders barter for it? Will they divide it up among the merchants?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Can you fill its hide with harpoons or its head with fishing spears?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: If you lay a hand on it, you will remember the struggle and never do it again!

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Any hope of subduing it is false; the mere sight of it is overpowering.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: No one is fierce enough to rouse it. Who then is able to stand against me?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Who has a claim against me that I must pay? Everything under heaven belongs to me.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: “I will not fail to speak of Leviathan`s limbs, its strength and its graceful form.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Who can strip off its outer coat? Who can penetrate its double coat of armor?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Who dares open the doors of its mouth, ringed about with fearsome teeth?

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Its back has rows of shields tightly sealed together;

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: each is so close to the next that no air can pass between.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: They are joined fast to one another; they cling together and cannot be parted.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Its snorting throws out flashes of light; its eyes are like the rays of dawn.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Flames stream from its mouth; sparks of fire shoot out.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Smoke pours from its nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Its breath sets coals ablaze, and flames dart from its mouth.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Strength resides in its neck; dismay goes before it.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: The folds of its flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Its chest is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: When it rises up, the mighty are terrified; they retreat before its thrashing.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: The sword that reaches it has no effect, nor does the spear or the dart or the javelin.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Iron it treats like straw and bronze like rotten wood.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Arrows do not make it flee; slingstones are like chaff to it.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: A club seems to it but a piece of straw; it laughs at the rattling of the lance.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Its undersides are jagged potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: It makes the depths churn like a boiling caldron and stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: It leaves a glistening wake behind it; one would think the deep had white hair.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: Nothing on earth is its equal— a creature without fear.

41.speaker: the-lord
41.quote: It looks down on all that are haughty; it is king over all that are proud.”

42.speaker: job
42.quote: “I know that you can do all things; no purpose of yours can be thwarted.

42.speaker: job
42.quote: You asked, ‘Who is this that obscures my plans without knowledge?` Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.

42.speaker: job
42.quote: “You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you shall answer me.`

42.speaker: job
42.quote: My ears had heard of you but now my eyes have seen you.

42.speaker: job
42.quote: Therefore I despise myself and repent in dust and ashes.”

42.speaker: the-lord
42.quote: “I am angry with you and your two friends, because you have not spoken the truth about me, as my servant Job has.

42.speaker: the-lord
42.quote: So now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. You have not spoken the truth about me, as my servant Job has.”
